title: All right, so one thing I've been considering is making the assistant process multi-tiered

text: All right, so one thing I've been considering is making the assistant process multi-tiered. The Sonnet medium can be the fastest execution. The second anything comes in, it automatically does what it needs to do, like these transcriptions appear instantly. The Sonnet level could then spawn another assistant. It's really a mastermind at that point, but it could be an Opus mastermind. One of the questions would be, should there just be one mastermind. The idea with the Opus is that you could speed things up. The Fable mastermind is bogged down, he's being real slow, he's got to relay things to minions and he can only do one task at a time. I'm not sure how we work in parallel, because once you separate into two masterminds, now we have to rely on a Sonnet or lesser model coordinating work between two more intelligent models. There might be a lack of understanding there, the left hand right hand parallelism might be too tricky. Now we could use worktrees, it's probably not a bad idea that each mastermind could create its own worktree, and then each mastermind with its own worktree could spawn minions to work on that worktree. I'm not sure how all those pointers would work. Each mastermind could create its own worktree, probably don't need a new worktree for each task, although a mastermind could spawn a minion that creates its own worktree if you wanted to branch off. When it comes to working in parallel to go faster, independent worktrees could be useful. However, if parallelism isn't really the issue and you can have different minions working on different things, then maybe that's better. However, I kind of actually like the idea of using sub worktrees. We could have multiple teams working on the same thing. Instead of just one mastermind or even three masterminds, we could have nine masterminds and each one decides how many minions and how to handle it. But they're essentially moving towards the same target. Once they create something that works, through all their reasoning and design process, they arrive at their conclusions, then you compare how they all work. I can see multiple versions and choose which one I like better.
